asof: Settles Wed 18 Nov 2026 · written Thu 19 Nov
headline: Hawkish minutes and Waller lift the front 1.5–3bp as 2028–29 rally; U7 peaks at 4.735%, still just over three hikes.
summary: SR3 bear-flattened at the front and bull-flattened at the back after the FOMC minutes: M7 rose 3bp in rate to 4.705%, H7 and U7 2.5bp to 4.57% and 4.735%, and Z6 1.5bp to 4.30%, while Z8 fell 3bp to 4.545% and Z9 4bp to 4.51%. Over the week U7 is still 8.5bp lower, Z7 10.5bp and Z8 13.5bp, against 0.5bp in Z6; from the 30 October settle H7 through U7 are 21.5–22.5bp higher, Z6 15.5bp and Z9 11.5bp. U7 remains the peak at 4.735%, 81.5bp over the 3.92% SOFR fixing, with 22.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is a little over three hikes, above the two many economists expect and short of Waller's case for reversing last year's three cuts and possibly more.
drivers: Minutes and Waller lean towards faster hikes

The October minutes showed almost all officials expect further hikes, with a couple open to 50bp in December if inflation data disappoint; Waller said a half-point move is probably needed unless the Fed signals January. M7 rose 3bp and H7 2.5bp, and Z6/H7 widened 1bp to +27bp.
Oil and AI-debt worries pull the back end lower

Brent settled $1.19 lower at $91.95 and WTI $2.75 lower at $83.26 after larger-than-expected inventory builds, and the minutes flagged opaque AI-related debt as a stability risk. Treasuries rallied for a third day with the 10-year near 5.08%, and Z8 to Z9 fell 3–4bp, taking U7/Z8 down 5.5bp to −19bp.
Housing mixed; 20-year auction on the screen

October starts jumped 9.9% to 1.309m against 1.25m expected, but permits fell 7.4% to 1.295m, the lowest since May 2020, against about 1.375m forecast. The $16bn 20-year sold at 5.459%, in line with when-issued, with a 2.63 bid-to-cover.
Funding steady ahead of bill settlement
SOFR fixed at 3.92% on 17 November, down 1bp but 4bp over EFFR at 3.88%, with reverse repo usage at $0.351bn. $300bn of 4-, 8- and 17-week bills settle on 24 November; U6 edged up 0.5bp to 3.9325%.
spreads: The front steepened into the peak while the post-peak inversion deepened. U6/Z6 rose 1bp to +36.75bp (+14.5bp on the month), Z6/H7 1bp to +27bp (−2.5bp week-to-date, +6bp on the month) and H7/M7 0.5bp to +13.5bp (−3.5bp on the week, +1bp on the month), while M7/U7 slipped 0.5bp to +3bp. Past the peak U7/Z7 fell 1.5bp to −4bp, Z7/H8 1.5bp to −5bp and H8/M8 1bp to −4bp, with the 2029 spreads between −1.5bp and 0. Z6/Z7 eased 0.5bp to +39.5bp (−10bp on the week, +4.5bp on the month) while Z6/M7 rose 1.5bp to +40.5bp (−6bp on the week, +7bp on the month); Z7/Z8 fell 4bp to −15bp (−7.5bp on the month) and U7/Z8 5.5bp to −19bp (−5bp on the week, −9bp on the month), and Z8/Z9 1bp to −3.5bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly rose 1bp to +10.5bp (−1.5bp on the week, +2bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 1bp to +7bp (+0.5bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Tuesday's (before the minutes), prices 26.1bp for 9 December (95.7% for 25bp, 4.3% for 50bp), 43.5bp by January, 60.1bp by March, 74.4bp by June and an 82.5bp peak by October 2027 (implied EFFR 4.705%), easing to 75.5bp by December 2027. That compares with 26.1bp, 44.5bp, 62.2bp, 78.8bp and an 85bp peak on Monday, 27.5bp, 42.5bp, 59.1bp, 72.1bp and 72.5bp a week earlier on 10 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 8.5bp on the month and the peak 25.5bp, though the peak is 2.5bp below Monday. Adding the 4bp SOFR–EFFR gap, Tuesday's ZQ path implies 4.30% for Z6's December–March window and 4.75% for U7, so Z6 at 4.30% matches and U7 at 4.735% sits 1.5bp below, even after Wednesday's 2.5bp rise. Many economists expect two hikes, while Waller wants the three 2025 cuts reversed and possibly more; the strip sits between the two, a little over three hikes.

ideas.title: Z6/M7: keep the re-sell order at +42bp
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3M7 (sell the Z6/M7 spread) at +42bp
ideas.why: The +42bp re-entry has not filled: the spread rose 1.5bp to +40.5bp on the minutes, still 6bp below last Friday and 7bp up on the month. A 50bp December hike or a clear January signal, as Waller wants, front-loads tightening into Z6 and narrows the spread. From +42bp it is 7bp to target against 4.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: If the gradualists spread hikes into mid-2027, M7's rate could rise faster than Z6's and push the spread through +46.5bp.

ideas.title: Hold long Z6/H7 into PCE
ideas.trade: Buy SR3Z6, sell SR3H7 (buy the Z6/H7 spread)
ideas.why: Open and 1bp in our favour: Z6/H7 rose 1bp to +27bp as the minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes. Tuesday's ZQ path prices 34bp across the January and March meetings, short of the hike-a-meeting pace Waller and Musalem argue for. From here it is 5bp to target and 5bp to the stop, 6bp against 4bp from entry.
ideas.risk: A soft PCE print or a deeper AI-led equity selloff could take early 2027 hikes out and push the spread below +22bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract into bill settlement and month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 rose 0.5bp in rate to 3.9325% while SOFR fixed at 3.92% on 17 November, 4bp over EFFR at 3.88%. Only its last week follows the 9 December decision, where Tuesday's ZQ priced a 4.3% chance of 50bp, and $300bn of bills settle on 24 November ahead of month-end with reverse repo usage near zero.
ideas.risk: If month-end passes quietly and SOFR slips back towards 3.88–3.90%, U6 would gain a couple of bp.
